jobs.title: Senior Access Management Engineer - Duo / MFA Specialist (Remote in the U.S.)
jobs.excerpt: GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk.
jobs.description:
GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. By taking a three-tiered, holistic approach for evaluating security posture and ecosystems, GuidePoint enables some of the nation’s top organizations, such as Fortune 500 companies and U.S. government agencies, to identify threats, optimize resources and integrate best-fit solutions that mitigate risk.

General Description

GuidePoint Security is hiring a Senior Access Management Engineer specializing in Cisco Duo to join our implementation team on a full-time basis. This is a fully remote role where we are looking for deep, hands-on experience leading Duo Security deployments, migrations, and integrations — with secondary proficiency in Okta and/or Ping Identity platforms to support broader Access Management engagements.

The Senior Access Management Engineer is responsible for designing, deploying, integrating, and optimizing Duo MFA and access solutions for some of the largest organizations in the US. This role serves as the go-to technical lead for all Duo engagements, owning architecture decisions, integration design, and delivery execution. When Duo engagements are not fully utilizing capacity, this resource will flex into a supporting engineer role on Okta and Ping Identity projects, contributing hands-on technical work under the direction of the engagement's lead architect.

This role sits at the intersection of security, infrastructure, and application integration — ensuring that multi-factor authentication, device trust, and adaptive access policies are implemented securely, reliably, and at scale.

About the Access Management practice

Coming to the Access Management team means working on the leading edge in the IAM space. As a Senior Access Management Engineer, you will be partnering with other engineers and architects to help some of the largest companies in the US implement their own identity and access management programs. From participating in assessments to full delivery of IAM platforms, you can expect to be involved at all levels of interaction with our customers. Your leadership and expertise are critical to providing our customers with the guidance they need, and the excellence they expect from GuidePoint Security.

We partner with the largest vendors in the space to ensure that the latest training is always available to our team. High level communication and collaboration are the standard. Mentorship at all levels, from Senior Architects to Junior Engineers, is foundational to our culture. We don't just talk about work life balance; we facilitate it with an unlimited PTO benefit.

We understand that in order to retain our talented team, leadership must provide regular feedback and coaching. We recruit new members to the team with the understanding that opportunities for growth are important. Whether your goals include future leadership opportunities, becoming an Architect or even moving to another discipline within security in time, the leadership team is focused on partnering with you to help achieve them.

Roles and Responsibilities:

Duo Security – Lead Engineer (Primary – 50%)

  • Serve as the primary technical lead on all Duo Security engagements, owning end-to-end delivery from design through implementation and handoff
  • Lead Duo deployment architecture and design, including:
    • Duo MFA — Policy design, user enrollment strategies, self-service portal configuration, and phased rollout planning
    • Duo Authentication Proxy — Deployment, configuration, high availability, and integration with RADIUS, LDAP, and Active Directory
    • Duo Single Sign-On (SSO) — SAML 2.0 and OIDC federation, application onboarding, and custom login branding
    • Duo Device Trust — Trusted endpoint policies, certificate-based device verification, and managed/unmanaged device posture enforcement
    • Duo Network Gateway (DNG) — Clientless remote access to internal web applications and SSH/RDP resources
    • Duo Admin Panel & API — Tenant configuration, Admin API and Auth API integrations, custom scripting, and reporting
    • Duo Trusted Endpoints — Integration with endpoint management platforms (Intune, Jamf, Workspace ONE, etc.)
    • Duo Desktop (formerly Duo Device Health) — Endpoint health verification and posture-based access policies
  • Design and implement Duo integrations across a wide range of application and infrastructure types, including:
    • VPN concentrators (Cisco ASA, Palo Alto GlobalProtect, Fortinet, Pulse/Ivanti)
    • Remote access platforms (Citrix, VMware Horizon, RD Gateway/NPS)
    • Web applications via SAML/OIDC federation or Duo Web SDK
    • Cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) for console and CLI MFA
    • On-premises infrastructure (Windows RDP, SSH, local OS logon)
    • Custom and legacy applications via Duo Auth API and Web SDK
  • Plan and execute Duo-to-Duo migrations (e.g., tenant consolidation) and competitive migrations from Duo to Okta, Duo to Entra ID, or other MFA platforms
  • Develop automation scripts (Python, PowerShell, Bash) leveraging Duo Admin API for bulk operations, reporting, user lifecycle management, and integration testing
  • Design phased MFA rollout strategies with user communication plans, pilot groups, and exception handling workflows
  • Conduct security reviews of Duo configurations, identifying gaps in policy coverage, authentication bypass risks, and device trust enforcement
  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, architecture diagrams, integration runbooks, and client-facing knowledge transfer materials

Okta & Ping Identity – Supporting Engineer (Secondary – 35%)

  • Serve as a supporting engineer on Okta and Ping Identity engagements when Duo workload permits, working under the direction of the engagement's lead architect
  • Contribute hands-on technical work on Okta engagements, including:
    • Application integration (SAML, OIDC, SWA) and SSO configuration
    • MFA policy configuration and adaptive access policies
    • Lifecycle Management (LCM) — provisioning, deprovisioning, and group-based automation
    • Directory integrations (Active Directory, LDAP, HR systems via SCIM)
    • Okta Workflows — supporting flow development for custom integrations and automations
    • User migration and bulk import operations
  • Contribute hands-on technical work on Ping Identity engagements, including:
    • PingFederate — SP/IdP connection configuration, adapter setup, and federation troubleshooting
    • PingOne — SSO, MFA, and directory service configuration
    • PingAccess — Resource and policy configuration for web application protection
    • On-premises Ping product support — Assisting with deployments, upgrades, and patching under architect direction
  • Execute assigned integration tasks, configuration changes, and testing activities with quality and consistency
  • Participate in peer reviews, knowledge-sharing sessions, and cross-training to deepen Okta and Ping Identity skills over time

Project Ownership & Client Success (10%)

  • Serve as the technical project owner on Duo engagements, taking full accountability for successful delivery and client outcomes
  • On Okta/Ping engagements, support the lead architect with clear status updates, task completion, and proactive communication of blockers
  • Delegate routine Duo tasks to junior engineers when available, providing clear direction and technical guidance
  • Mentor junior resources through hands-on pairing, configuration reviews, and knowledge-sharing sessions
  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, architecture diagrams, implementation guides, and runbooks for all engagements
  • Contribute to the development of standard operating procedures (SOPs), delivery templates, and Duo-specific best practice frameworks

At Colibri, culture is a critical part of our collective success, and we live our values everyday: Love, Joy,
Boldness, Teamwork and Curiosity. These values guide our interactions with each other, our customers,
and the community as a whole.
We have a rich and storied history. Colibri is one of the pioneers of online professional education,
introducing some of the first web-based professional education courses in 2001. Today, the company’s
family of brands are the leading online professional education platforms in their respective end-markets.
We proudly serve >1 million customers annually and employ more than 1,500 mission-aligned
professionals. To learn more, please visit:

Position Overview:

Colibri Group is seeking a practical, business-oriented Commercial Contracts Attorney to join its
Legal, Regulatory and Compliance team. Reporting to the General Counsel, this attorney will play a
lead role in the review, drafting and negotiation of a broad range of commercial agreements
supporting Colibri’s businesses and corporate functions.

The role is intentionally broad. Colibri contracts both as a provider of products and services and as
a purchaser of technology, services, content and other goods and services. The successful
candidate therefore should be an experienced commercial generalist who is comfortable moving
between customer-facing and vendor-side agreements rather than specializing in a single contract
type or business model.

In addition to handling commercial transactions, this attorney will help improve and bring greater
structure to Colibri’s contracting function. This includes developing templates and negotiation
playbooks, establishing consistent contracting and escalation practices, improving contract intake
and lifecycle-management processes, and helping Colibri more effectively use its AI-enabled
contract management technology.

The Commercial Contracts Attorney will also supervise and develop members of the contracts team,
including Contract Specialists, and will work closely with colleagues across Sales, Finance,
Procurement, Privacy, Information Security, Technology, Product, Marketing, Human Resources
and other business functions.

What You'll Do

    Commercial Contracting
    • Draft, review and negotiate a broad range of commercial agreements on both the customer
    and vendor sides of transactions, including master services agreements, statements of work,
    order forms, subscription and technology agreements, software and SaaS agreements,
    professional and consulting services agreements, licensing agreements, content
    agreements, marketing agreements, distribution and referral agreements, data processing
    agreements, confidentiality agreements and other commercial arrangements.
    • Independently manage routine and moderately complex commercial negotiations from
    intake through execution, identifying material legal and business risks and developing
    practical solutions that enable the business to achieve its objectives.
    • Exercise sound judgment in determining when an issue can be resolved within established
    parameters and when a matter should be escalated to the General Counsel or another
    subject-matter expert.
    • Translate business objectives and operational requirements into clear contractual terms
    and explain contractual risks and alternatives to business stakeholders in practical,
    understandable terms.
    • Partner closely with business teams to understand the commercial context of transactions
    and distinguish material legal and business risks from issues that do not warrant delaying or
    disrupting a transaction.

    Contracting Operations and Process Improvement
    • Help design and implement a more consistent and scalable contracting function, including
    contract intake, review, approval, signature, storage, renewal and post-execution processes.
    • In partnership with the General Counsel, develop and maintain contract templates, clause
    libraries, negotiation guidance, contracting playbooks and escalation standards to promote
    consistency and enable appropriate delegation of contract review.
    • Take an active role in the administration, optimization and adoption of Colibri’s AI-enabled
    contract lifecycle management and contract review technology, including identifying
    opportunities to automate routine work, improve contract visibility and reduce manual
    processes.
    • Evaluate existing contracting practices and identify practical improvements to workflow,
    documentation, reporting, approval processes and allocation of work within the Legal team.
    • Develop appropriate metrics and reporting to provide visibility into contract volume, cycle
    times, status, recurring negotiation issues, renewal obligations and other useful contracting
    information.
    • Maintain reliable contract records and promote consistent use of the Company’s contract
    repository and related systems.
    • Identify recurring contractual issues and use those trends to recommend changes to
    templates, guidance, training or business processes.
    Team Leadership and Stakeholder Support
    • Provide day-to-day supervision, coaching and development to internal contract specialists.
    • Establish clear expectations regarding which matters may be handled by contract
    specialists, which require attorney review and which require escalation to the General
    Counsel or other subject-matter experts.
    • Review and support the work of contract specialists on contract administration, routine
    negotiations and related contracting activities

What You'll Need to Succeed

    • Juris Doctor from an accredited law school.
    • Active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar.
    • Approximately 5–8 years of relevant legal experience, including meaningful responsibility for
    drafting and negotiating commercial agreements. A combination of law firm and in-house
    experience is acceptable.
    • Demonstrated experience negotiating agreements from both the customer and
    vendor/procurement perspectives, or sufficiently broad commercial contracting experience
    to work effectively on both sides of transactions.
    • Substantive experience independently negotiating data processing agreements and privacy
    and data-protection provisions in commercial contracts.
    • Working knowledge of major privacy and data protection concepts applicable to commercial
    transactions, including GDPR and U.S. state privacy requirements.
    • Experience using a contract lifecycle management system or comparable contract
    management technology.
    • Experience using AI-enabled contract review, drafting, analysis or contract-management
    tools, with an interest in using technology to improve the quality and efficiency of legal
    services.
    • Experience supervising, mentoring or directing the work of contract specialists, paralegals
    or other legal professionals.
    • Demonstrated ability to independently manage a meaningful volume of contracts with
    competing deadlines and varying levels of complexity.

Preferred Qualifications

    • Prior in-house legal experience.
    • Experience implementing, materially improving or administering a contract lifecycle
    management system.
    • Experience helping create or refine contract templates, clause libraries, negotiation
    playbooks, approval matrices or escalation procedures.
    • Experience working in an organization with multiple business units, products or service
    offerings and a correspondingly diverse portfolio of commercial agreements.
    • Experience improving a contracting environment that previously relied heavily on manual
    processes or decentralized practices.
    • Familiarity with commercial technology, intellectual property, information security and AIrelated contractual issues

What Success Looks like

    • Experience implementing, materially improving or administering a contract lifecycle
    management system.
    • Experience helping create or refine contract templates, clause libraries, negotiation
    playbooks, approval matrices or escalation procedures.
    • Experience working in an organization with multiple business units, products or service
    offerings and a correspondingly diverse portfolio of commercial agreements.
    • Experience improving a contracting environment that previously relied heavily on manual
    processes or decentralized practices.

jobs.description:
About AllVoices

AllVoices is the AI-native employee relations platform. We give HR and ER teams one system for intake, case management, investigations, and analytics, backed by a whistleblower hotline trusted by companies like Sweetgreen, Panera Bread, and Harbor Freight. Employee relations has run on spreadsheets, inboxes, and institutional memory. We are replacing that with a platform that makes the work faster, more consistent, and defensible.

Senior Director, Product Marketing

Location: Remote (US) | Department: Marketing | Reports to: Chief Revenue Officer

The Role

We are hiring a Senior Director of Product Marketing to own how AllVoices is positioned, differentiated, and understood in market. You will define who we sell to and why they should choose us, then carry that through every surface it shows up on: the website, the sales deck, the competitive brief, the launch, and the customer communication.

This is a hands-on role in a lean team. You will set strategy and also build the deck, write the script, and brief the designer. It sits close to Sales, close to Product, and close to the number.

What You'll Do

Own ICP definition and value proposition

This is the primary responsibility of the role. Maintain a clear, current definition of who we sell to, and the value propositions that land with each buyer and segment. Keep that definition sharp as we move upmarket and as the ER category evolves, and make sure every other function is working from the same version of it.

Own competitive differentiation

Maintain competitive assessments across the ER and HR tech landscape. Define how we differentiate, and translate that into positioning Sales can use in live deals. Claims must be defensible and differentiation honest.

Ground positioning in buyer and deal evidence

Run the research that keeps positioning honest: win/loss analysis, buyer interviews, and the qualitative signal coming out of sales conversations. Bring findings back to Sales, Product, and leadership as evidence, and use them to refine ICP, messaging, and value props.

Own website messaging and conversion

Own the homepage, product pages, and company-wide messaging. Translate value and competitive differentiation into content that converts, and work with design and development partners to ship changes and test them. Treat the site as a conversion asset with owned metrics, not a brochure.

Own product launches

Run the go-to-market motion for releases: launch tiering, positioning and naming, messaging, enablement, and the cross-functional calendar. Partner with Product so what ships is understood by the market, and Sales and customers hear about it in a coordinated way.

Partner on audience and paid strategy

Work with media agencies on audience strategy, and build audiences alongside RevOps and Marketing Ops. Partner with designers to keep creative best in class, and hold agency output to the same messaging standard as everything else we publish.

Partner with Events, Content, and Community and Partnerships

Work with the Head of Events, Content, and Community to make sure the topics we program against are the ones our ICP cares most about. Bring the buyer, market, and competitive insight that shapes editorial and event themes, and keep that work anchored to our positioning.

Create content directly

Build what the moment needs: decks, one-pagers, and simple ad creative using Canva and Claude Design. Comfort producing polished work yourself, quickly, is a requirement of this role. We also work with freelance designers as needed.

Own sales enablement content

Own the Sales Resource Library, which is used heavily across every deal. Maintain sales decks, business case materials, video assets, and competitive collateral, and train the team on how and when to use them. Use performance data and sales insight to decide what to build, retire, and refresh, and partner closely with Sales and the leadership team on where the gaps are.

Manage quarterly customer webinars

Manage the quarterly customer webinar and build the outline and script Product presents from: what shipped last quarter, what is coming next, and why it matters to their work. Own the format and flow so it is easy to follow and worth the hour.

Own customer product communications

Draft the weekly customer newsletter in close partnership with Product, so customers know what is new, what they may have missed, and what is coming soon. Use in-app messaging to reach the right audience with major releases.

What You Bring

  • 8+ years in B2B SaaS product marketing, including ownership of positioning and messaging for a full product line
  • Built ICP and value proposition frameworks that Sales actually used, not documents that sat in a drive
  • Strong competitive marketing background, including running assessments and equipping a sales team to win against named competitors
  • Owned website messaging and worked with design and development partners to ship and test it
  • Ran product launches end to end across Product, Sales, and Marketing
  • Built sales enablement assets, partnership materials, and train reps on them, with evidence they moved deals
  • Hands-on production ability. Canva, AI tooling, and comfort building decks and creative yourself
  • Strong writer. Clear, direct, and able to move between a competitive brief, ad copy, and a customer newsletter
  • Experience marketing to HR, Legal, or Compliance buyers preferred
  • Comfortable in a lean team where strategy and execution sit in the same person

Benefits

Who We Are
DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers operate in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production.

The Opportunity

Cloud spend is no longer just AWS, Google Cloud and Azure. Our customers now run a large and growing share of their technology spend through SaaS platforms, data clouds and AI vendors - and every one of those vendors is an integration that brings another slice of their spend into view.

You'll own DoiT's Integrations Framework and the experience built on top of it. This is a chance to define what a great integration experience looks like: a customer connects a new vendor in minutes, sees at a glance that their data is flowing, and handles credential rotation, reconnects and backfills themselves without thinking twice. On the framework side, you'll make adding the next vendor a small, well-understood piece of work rather than a project - so coverage grows as fast as the vendor landscape does.

You'll work AI-augmented from day one. Integration development is spec-driven work against constantly changing third-party APIs: one of the highest-leverage places to apply agentic AI tooling. We expect you to use it across your whole workflow and to have real opinions about where it earns its place.

Responsibilities

  • Building new integrations. This is the core of the role. Design and ship integrations against third-party billing and usage APIs - authentication, incremental sync, rate limits, error handling, schema drift - and invest in the Integrations Framework itself, along with testing harnesses and scaffolding, so the tenth integration takes a fraction of the effort of the first.

Push on what agentic tooling can do for this codebase, and bring judgement about where AI raises velocity and where a human still has to hold the quality bar.
